Monday actions: tiering, hardening and detection
Legacy, PAC validation, segmentation and response

takeaways: Active Directory drifts toward insecurity through convenience: unconstrained delegation, stale KRBTGT keys, overprivileged backup accounts and shared local admin passwords each open a quiet path to domain dominance.

Close those paths with constrained or resource-based delegation, twice-rotated KRBTGT, gMSAs, Windows LAPS, SMB signing, LSA protection and Credential Guard, and remove GPP passwords, open trusts and loose certificate templates.
Enforce tiering with privileged access workstations, tune detections on Kerberos, replication and LSASS events, and run contained, evidence-first response rituals instead of improvised clean-ups.
hook: Active Directory rarely fails loudly; it drifts, one exception and one forgotten service account at a time, until an attacker walks a quiet path to domain admin. This episode is for identity, infrastructure and security teams who run on-premises AD. It walks through the most common misconfigurations, the attack chains they enable and the hardening, tiering and detection rituals that close them.
